plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Direction/magnitude of gain, lag, and noise level, which determine basic controllability and what u holds the 0.5 target.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with self-cooling and lag is correct, y rises monotonically from ~0.078 with a lag of tens of seconds, still rising at 180s but with declining slope, reaching roughly 0.25-0.45 and showing low noise.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Second-amplitude gain and steady-state input needed to hold y=0.5, which sets controller feedforward and whether 0.3 holds the target.
experiments.expected_observation: If high-gain slow first-order hypothesis is right (tau ~200-300s, u_star ~0.3), y starting at 0.443 will flatten and drift slowly up toward ~0.45-0.51 over 180s with slope dropping toward 0-0.0005, staying below 0.55 with low noise; if instead gain is low, y will clearly decay.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: How output behaves at u=0 (decay rate, ambient, cooling time constant) which determines integral action, overshoot recovery, and feedforward.
experiments.expected_observation: If slow first-order with tau ~150-250s and ambient ~0.07-0.09 is right, y will decay monotonically from ~0.42 to ~0.20-0.25 over 180s with declining negative slope still ~-0.0007 to -0.0012 at end (not settled), low noise; if cooling is much faster, y will fall below 0.15 by end.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input needed to hold y=0.5 and linearity near the target band, which sets feedforward and whether 0.4 settles inside the band.
experiments.expected_observation: If tau~150s, gain~1.14 and ambient~0.08 is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.185 toward ~0.53 equilibrium, reaching ~0.40-0.46 after 180s with last-5s slope still positive ~0.0005-0.001 and low noise, staying well below 0.6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain/equilibrium at u=0.4 near the target and settling time constant, which sets feedforward u-star and PI tuning to hold 0.5 without overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If tau~150-160s, ambient~0.08, gain~1.07 (y_ss~0.51 at u=0.4) is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.405 toward ~0.47-0.48 after 180s with slope declining from ~0.0014 to ~0.0005-0.0008, staying below 0.55 with quantization steps ~0.005; if gain is much higher y will exceed 0.50, if much lower it will flatten below 0.45.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state equilibrium at u=0.4 near the target and settling time constant, which sets feedforward u-star and PI tuning to hold 0.5 without overshoot.
experiments.expected_observation: If tau~159s, ambient~0.078, gain~1.08 (y_ss~0.508 at u=0.4) is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.475 toward ~0.508, reaching ~0.49-0.495 after 150s with slope declining to ~0.0001-0.0002 and quantization steps ~0.005, staying below 0.55; if equilibrium is lower (~0.475 settled) y will stay flat at ~0.475.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: u=0 cooling rate and pure delay, which isolates increased heat loss and delay change from pure actuator weakening and sensor change and determines retuning.
experiments.expected_observation: If faster-outflow leading hypothesis is right, after a short <15s delay y will fall monotonically from ~0.4 and clearly faster than E3, dropping >0.09 in first 60s and reaching ~0.08-0.13 after 300s with low noise and ~0.005 quantization; if only actuator weakened with unchanged cooling, the fall will overlay E3 shifted to 0.4 start with slope ~-0.0013 and reach ~0.12-0.16.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: New heating gain and steady-state u to hold y=0.5 under increased loss, which sets retuning and discriminates faster-outflow magnitude from pure actuator weakening and slow response by comparing rise from ~0.094 at u=0.5 directly to E1.
experiments.expected_observation: If faster-outflow (C2) is right with ~2x loss and tau ~70-90s, y rises promptly after <15s delay from ~0.094 toward a lower equilibrium ~0.28-0.36, reaching ~0.28-0.36 after 240s with flattening slope and same ~0.005 quantization/low noise, clearly below E1 trajectory (0.443 at 180s) and below 0.5; if only weaker actuator with unchanged cooling, rise would be slower and equilibrium higher than this but cooling in E7 would have matched E3, which it did not; if much slower response, first 30-60s would stay flat near 0.094 before rising.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: New high-u steady-state gain and u-star to hold y=0.5 under increased loss, which sets retuning feedforward and whether target is reachable without saturation.
experiments.expected_observation: If faster-outflow C2 is right with tau ~70-95s and y_ss(0.5)~0.30, y will rise promptly within <15s from ~0.298 toward ~0.43-0.46 equilibrium, reaching ~0.38-0.43 after 110s with flattening slope and same ~0.005 quantization/low noise, staying well below 0.6; if only weaker actuator, rise would extrapolate to much higher equilibrium and cooling in E7 would have matched E3, which it did not; if much slower response, first 30-60s would stay flat near 0.30 before rising.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Magnitude of increased heat loss / new high-u steady-state gain and u-star to hold y=0.5, which sets retuning feedforward and whether target is reachable without saturation.
experiments.expected_observation: If faster-outflow C2 is right with tau ~70-95s and y_ss(0.8)~0.42-0.46, y will rise promptly from ~0.40 (delay already elapsed after 110s at 0.8) toward ~0.42-0.45, reaching ~0.42-0.44 after 85s with flattening slope to ~0 and same ~0.005 quantization/low noise, staying below 0.50; if much slower response, rise would be delayed/flat then steep, which E9 already rules out.

ledger.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y with positive gain (heater heats the sensor).

Step response has small delay ~6-15s plus slow first-order-like approach with dominant time constant ~150-170s originally; E7 shows delay still short (<15s, immediate fall) and E8/E9 show prompt rise (<10s, E9 rise within 8s) but approach now faster tau ~70-95s, so original tau no longer holds for changed machine.

There is no large dead-zone: u=0.3, 0.4 and 0.5 all produce clearly measurable heating versus u=0, and changed machine E8 shows u=0.5 still heats from 0.094 to ~0.293 and E9 shows u=0.8 heats from 0.298 to 0.40.

At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.07-0.09 with cooling tau ~150-160s. E7 from 0.40 fell >0.12 in first 60s to 0.094 after 300s, much faster than E3 (0.421 to 0.185 in 180s), so this tau is falsified for the changed machine.

Steady-state y was approximately linear in u over 0-0.5 with gain ~1.05-1.12 (y_ss ~0.08+1.07*u) originally: E1 0.5 rising toward ~0.61, E2 0.3 near ~0.40, E4+E5+E6 0.4 settled at ~0.497. Changed machine holds much lower level for same u: E8 0.5 settles ~0.29-0.33 after 240s vs 0.443 at 180s in E1, and E9 0.8 reaches only 0.40 after 110s vs ~0.94 expected originally.

The steady-state u needed to hold y=0.5 was ~0.39-0.40 originally, because u=0.4 held for 510s settles at 0.497. After change y fell from 0.49 to 0.36 despite u rising 0.39 to 0.74, and E8 shows u=0.5 holds only ~0.30 and E9 shows u=0.8 holds only ~0.40-0.43 after 110s, so this u-star is falsified for changed machine; new u-star is much higher ~0.9-1.0.

Sensor noise/std is small (<0.01) compared to control band width 0.05, with quantization steps ~0.005. E7 and E8/E9 show same steps and low noise, no large offset (E7 settles ~0.094 vs 0.07-0.09, E8/E9 rises smooth).
Change is weaker actuator: same u produces smaller temperature rise, but u=0 cooling rate, delay and sensor characteristics are unchanged.

Change is faster outflow / larger heat loss: u=0 decay is faster than E3 and same u holds a lower level, consistent with y falling from 0.49 to 0.36 despite u rising from 0.39 to 0.74 and E7 dropping 0.40 to 0.094 in 300s and E8 holding only ~0.293 at u=0.5 after 240s and E9 holding only ~0.40 at u=0.8 after 110s, implying gain ~0.42-0.44 and ambient ~0.08-0.09.
Change is much slower response: delay or dominant tau greatly increased, so y keeps falling long after u is raised before recovering.
Change is sensor offset or much larger noise: true thermal dynamics and gain unchanged, only reading shifted or noisier.
